verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> he began to speake to them in parables, <na>[2]</na> A man planted a vineyard and made a hedge about it, and digged a trough, and built a tovvre, and let it out to husbandmen: and vvent forth into a strange countrie.

notes.text: This man, is God the Father. This vineyard, is (as Esay saith 5, 1.) the house of Israel. The seruants sent, are Moyses and the Prophets, whom the Iewes did diuersely afflict and persecute.

verses.text: And he sent to the husbandmen in season a seruant, to receiue of the husbandmen, of the fruite of the vineyard.
Who apprehending him, bette him: and sent him avvay emptie.
And againe he sent to them an other seruant: and him they wounded in the head, and vsed him reprochefully.
And againe he sent an other, and him they killed: and many other, beating certaine, and killing others.
Therfore hauing yet one <na>[1]</na> sonne most deere: him also he sent vnto them last saying, That they vvill reuerence my sonne.

notes.text: His Sonne is CHRIST our Sauiour, whō the Iewes crucified out of the citie of Ierusalem, as it were casting him out of the vineyard.

verses.text: But the husbandmen said one to an other, This is the heier: come, let vs kill him: and the inheritance shal be ours.
And apprehending him, they killed him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard.
What therfore vvil the lord of the vineyard doe? <na>[1]</na> He vvil come and destroy the husbandmen: and vvil giue the vineyard to others.

notes.text: The Iewes and their guides to whom the vineyard was set, destroied: and Gods vineyard giuen to the Apostles and their Successors in the Gentils.

verses.text: Neither haue you read this scripture, [1] The [2] stone which the builders reiected, the same is made the head of the corner:

notes.text: CHRIST is become the corner stone of the Synagogue and the Church in which the faithful both of the Iewes and Gentils are conteined.

verses.text: By our Lord was this done, and it is maruelous in our eies?
And they sought to lay hands on him, and they feared the multitude. for they knevv that he spake this parable to them. And leauing him they vvent their way.
<cr>[1]</cr> And they send to him certaine of the Pharisees and of the Herodians: that they should entrappe him in his vvord.

VVho comming, say to him, Maister, vve knovv that thou art a true speaker, and carest not for any man: for thou doest not looke vpon the person of men, but teachest the vvay of God in truth. is it lavvful to giue tribute to Cæsar: or shal vve not giue it?
Who knovving their subteltie, said to them, VVhy tempt you me? bring me a penie that I may see it.
But they brought it him. And he saith to them, VVhose is this image, and inscription? They say to him, Cæsars.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said to them, Render therfore the things that are Cæsars, to Cæsar: and that are Gods, to God. And they marueled at him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> there came to him the Saducees that say there is no resurrection: and they asked him saying, Maister,
<cr>[1]</cr> Moyses vvrote vnto vs, that if any mans brother die, and leaue his wife, and leaue no children, his brother shal take his vvife and raise vp seede to his brother.
There vvere therfore seuen brethren: and the first tooke a vvife, and died leauing no issue.
And the second tooke her, and died: and neither this left issue. And the third in like maner.
And the seuen tooke her in like sort: and did not leaue issue. Last of al the vvoman also died.
In the resurrection therfore vvhen they shal rise againe, vvhose vvife shal she be of these? for the seuen had her to vvife.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said to them, Do ye not therfore erre , not knovving the scriptures, nor the povver of God?
For vvhen they shal rise againe from the dead, they shal neither marrie, nor be married, but are as the Angels in heauen.

And as concerning the dead, that they do rise againe, haue you not read in the booke of Moyses, hovv in the bush God spake to him, saying, [1] I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the liuing. You therfore are much deceiued.
And <cr>[1]</cr> there came one of the Scribes that had heard them questioning, and seeing that he had wel answered them, asked him vvhich vvas the first commaundement of al.
And IESVS answered him, That the first commaundement of al is, [1] Heare Israel: the Lord thy God, is one God.
And thou shalt loue the Lord thy God from thy vvhole hart, and with thy vvhole soul, and vvith thy vvhole minde, and vvith thy vvhole povver. This is the first commaundement.
And the second is like to it, [1] Thou shalt loue they neighbour as thy self. An other commaundement greater then these there is not.
And the Scribe said to him, VVel Maister, thou hast said in truth, that there is one God, and there is none other besides him.

And that he be loued from the vvhole hart, and vvith the vvhole vnderstanding, and vvith the vvhole soule, and vvith the vvhole strength: and <na>[1]</na> to loue his neighbour as him self is a greater thing then al holocaustes and sacrifices.

notes.text: This excellencie of Charitie teacheth vs that faith only is not sufficient.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> seeing that he had ansvvered vvisely, said to him, Thou art not farre from the kingdom of God. And no man novv durst aske him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said, teaching in the temple, Hovv do the Scribes say, that Christ is the sonne of Dauid?
For Dauid him self saith in the holy Ghost: [1] Our Lord said to my Lord, sit on my right hand, vntil I put thine enemies the foote-stoole of thy feete.
Dauid therfore him self calleth him Lord, and vvhence is he his sonne? And a great multitude heard him gladly.
And he said to them in his doctrine, Take heede of the Scribes that vvil vvalke in long robes, and be saluted in the market-place,
and sit in the first chaires in the Synagogs, and loue the highest places at suppers:
which deuoure vvidovves houses vnder the pretence of long prayer: these shal receiue larger iudgement.
<cr>[1]</cr> And <sc>IESVS</sc> sitting ouer against the treasurie, beheld how the multitude did cast money into the treasurie, and many rich men did cast in much.
And when there came a certaine poore widow, she cast in two mites, which is a farthing.
And calling his Disciples together, he saith to them, Amen I say to you, that this poore widow hath cast in <na>[1]</na> more then al that haue cast into the treasurie.

notes.text: God doth accept almes that are correspondent to euery mans abilitie: and the more able, the more must a man giue.

verses.text: For al they of their aboundance haue cast in: but she, of her penurie hath cast in al that she had, her whole liuing.

chapters.summary: He foretelleth to the Iewes in a parable their reprobation most worthy, and the vocation of the Church of the Gentils in their place, 10 him self being the headstone thereof. 13 He defeateth the snare of the Pharisees and Herodians, about paying tribute to Cæsar: 18 answereth also the inuention of the Sadducees against the Resurrection: 28 also the opposition of a Scribe. 35 And so hauing put al the busie sectes to silence, he turneth and poseth them on the other side, because they imagined Christ should be no more but a man. 38 Bidding the people to beware of the Scribes, being ambitious and hypocrites. 41 He commendeth the poore widow for her two mites, aboue al.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> vvhen he vvent out of the temple, one of his Disciples saith to him, Maister, behold what maner of stones, and vvhat kinde of buildings.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew c. 24.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said to him, Seest thou al these great buildings? There shal not be left a stone vpon a stone, that shal not be destroied.
And vvhen he sate in Mount-oliuet against the temple, Peter and Iames and Iohn and Andrevv asked him apart,
<na>[1]</na> Tel vs, vvhen shal these things be? and vvhat shal be the signe vvhen al these things shal begin to be consummate?

notes.text: TVESDAY night.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering began to say to them, See, that no man seduce you.
for many shal come in my name saying that I am he: and they shal seduce many.
<na>[1]</na> And vvhen you shal heare of vvarres and bruites of vvarres, feare not. for these things must be, but the end is not yet.

notes.text: Great warres toward the later end.

verses.text: For nation shal rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there shal be earthquakes in places, and famines. These things are the beginning of sorovves.

<na>[1]</na> But looke to your selues. For they shal deliuer you vp in Councels, and in Synagogs shal you be beaten, and you shal stand before Presidents and Kings for my sake, for a testimonie vnto them.

notes.text: Much persecution of the faithful and Catholike men in the later end.

verses.text: And into al nations first the Gospel must be preached.

And vvhen they shal leade you and deliuer you, be not careful before hand vvhat you shal speake: but that vvhich shal be giuen you in that houre, that speake ye. For it is not you that speake, but the holy Ghost.
<na>[1]</na> And brother shal deliuer brother vnto death, and the father his sonne: and the children shal arise against the parents, and shal vvorke their death.

notes.text: Great treacherie and many false brethren at the same time.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> And you shal be odious to al men for my name. But he that shal endure vnto the end, he shal be saued.

notes.text: Constancie and perseuerance necessarie in time of persecution.

verses.text: And when you shal see [1] the abomination of desolation, standing vvhere it ought not (he that readeth, let him vnderstand) then they that are in Ievvrie, let them flee vnto the mountaines:
and he that is on the house-toppe, let him not goe dovvne into the house, nor enter in to take any thing out of his house:
and he that shal be in the field, let him not returne backe to take his garment.
And vvo to them that are vvith childe and that giue sucke in those daies.
But pray that the things chaunce not in the vvinter.
For those daies shal be such tribulations as vvere not from the beginning of the creation that God created vntil novv, neither shal be.
And vnles the Lord had shortened the daies, no flesh should be saued: but for the elect vvhich he hath elected, he hath <na>[1]</na> shortened the daies.

notes.text: Antichrists reigne shalbe three yeres and a halfe. Dan. 7. Apoc. 13.

verses.text: And then if any man shal say vnto you, Loe, here is Christ: loe, there: do not beleeue.
For there shal rise vp false-Christs and false-Prophets, and they shal shevv signes and vvonders, to seduce (if it be possible) the elect also.
You therfore take heede: behold I haue foretold you al things.
But in those daies after that tribulation <cr>[1]</cr> the sunne shal be darkened, and the moone shal not giue her light,
and the starres of heauen shal be falling dovvne, and the povvers that are in heauen, shal be moued.
And then they shal see the <cr>[1]</cr> Sonne of man comming in the cloudes, vvith much povver and glorie.
And then shal he send his Angels, and shal gather together his elect from the foure vvindes, from the vttermost part of the earth to the vttermost part of heauen.
And of the figtree learne ye a parable. VVhen novv the bough thereof is tender, and the leaues come forth, you know that sommer is very nigh.
so you also vvhen you shal see these things come to passe, knovv ye that it is very nigh, at the doores.
Amen I say to you, that this generation shal not passe, vntil al these things be done.
Heauen and earth shal passe, but my vvordes shal not passe.
But of that day or houre no man knoweth, neither the Angels in heauen, nor the <na>[1]</na> Sonne, but the Father.

notes.text: Not as though him self knew not, as the Heretikes Agnoïtę held: but because he knew it not for to teach it others, as being not expedient. Ambr. de fide li. 5 c. 8.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Take heede, vvatch, and pray. for you know not vvhen the time is.

notes.text: And on the Anniversary of the creation of a Bishop.

verses.text: Euen as a man vvho being gone into a strange countrie, left his house: and gaue his seruants authoritie ouer ech vvorke, and commaunded the porter to vvatch.
VVatch ye therfore (for you knovv not vvhen the lord of the house commeth: at euen, or at midnight, or at the cocke crovving, or in the morning)
lest comming vpon a soden, he finde you sleeping.
And that vvhich I say to you, I say to al, Watch. ⊢

chapters.summary: To his Disciples (by occasion of Hierusalem and the Temples destruction) he foretelleth, 5 what things shalbe before the consummation of the world, as specially the Churches ful preaching vnto al nations. 14 Then, what shalbe in the very consummation, to wit, Antichrist with his passing great persecution and seduction, but for a short time. 24 then incontinent the day of Iudgement, 28 to our great comfort in those miseries vnder Antichrist. 32 As for the moment, to vs it perteineth not to know it. 33 but rather euery man to watch, that we be not vnprouided when he commeth to ech one particularly by death.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> the Pasche vvas and the Azymes after tvvo daies: and the cheefe Priests and the Scribes sought hovv they might by some vvile lay hands on him, and kil him.

notes.text: TENEBRÆ Wednesday.

verses.text: For they said, Not on the festiual day, lest there might be a tumult of the people.

And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen he vvas at Bethania in the house of Simon the Leper, and sate at meate, there came a vvoman hauing an alabaster boxe of ointment, of pretious spike-narde: and breaking the alabaster-boxe, she povvred it out vpon his head.
But there vvere certaine that had indignation vvithin them selues, and said, VVhereto is this vvast of the ointment made?
For this ointment might haue been sold for more then three hundred pence, and giuen to the poore. And they murmured against her.
But <sc>IESVS</sc> said, Let her alone, vvhy do you molest her? she hath vvrought a good vvorke vpon me.
for the poore you haue alvvaies vvith you: and vvhen you vvil, you may doe them good: but <na>[1]</na> me you haue not alvvaies.

notes.text: We haue not Christ here needing our almes, as when he conuersed vpon the earth. See Mat. 26, 11.

verses.text: That vvhich she had, she hath done: she hath preuented to anoint my body to the burial.
Amen I say to you, VVheresoeuer this Gospel shal be preached in the vvhole vvorld, that also vvhich she hath done, shal be told for a memorie for her.
And <cr>[1]</cr> Iudas Iscariote one of the Tvvelue vvent his vvay to the cheefe Priests, for to betray him to them.
Who hearing it, vvere glad: and they promised him that they vvould giue him money. And he sought hovv he might betray him conueniently.
<cr>[1]</cr> And <na>[2]</na> the first day of the Azymes vvhen they sacrificed the Pasche, the Disciples say to him, VVither vvilt thou that we goe, and prepare for thee to eate the Pasche?

notes.text: MAVNDY Thursday.

verses.text: And he sendeth tvvo of his Disciples, and saith to them, Goe ye into the citie: and there shal meete you a man carying a pitcher of water, folovv him:
and whithersoeuer he entreth, say to the maister of the house, that the Maister saith, Where is my refectorie, vvhere I may eate the Pasche vvith my Disciples?
And he vvil shevv you a great chamber, adorned: and there prepare for vs.
And his Disciples vvent their vvaies, and came into the citie: and they found as he had told them, and they prepared the Pasche.
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen euen vvas come, he commeth vvith the Tvvelue.
And vvhen they vvere sitting at the table and eating, <sc>IESVS</sc> said, Amen I say to you, that one of you shal betray me, he that eateth vvith me.
But they began to be sad, and to say to him seuerally, Is it I?
VVho said to them, One of the Tvvelue, he that dippeth vvith me his hand in the dish.
and the Sonne of man in deede goeth, <cr>[1]</cr> as it is vvritten of him, but vvo to that man by vvhom the Sonne of man shal be betrayed. it vvere good for him, if that man had not been borne.
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhiles they vvere eating, <sc>IESVS</sc> tooke bread: and blessing brake, and gaue to them, and said, Take, <sc>THIS IS MY BODY</sc>.
And taking the chalice, giuing thankes he gaue to them. and they <na>[1]</na> al dranke of it.

notes.text: Al dranke, to wit, al the twelue, for moe were not present. Whereby is euident that the wordes in S. Mat. (26, 27) Drinke ye al of this, were spoken to al the Apostles onely, which here are said that they al did drinke. And so it is no general commaundement to al men.

verses.text: And he said to them, <sc>THIS IS MY BLOVD OF THE NEVV TESTAMENT, THAT SHAL BE SHED FOR MANY</sc>.
Amen I say to you, that novv I vvil not drinke of the fruite <cr>[1]</cr> of the vine vntil that day vvhen I shal drinke it new in the kingdom of God.
<na>[1]</na> And an hymne being said, they vvent forth into Mountoliuet.

notes.text: THVRSDAY night.

verses.text: And IESVS saith to them, You shal al be scandalized in me in this night: for it is vvritten, [1] I vvil strike the Pastor, and the sheepe shal be dispersed.
But after that I shal be risen againe, I wil goe before you into Galilee.
And Peter said to him, Although al shal be scandalized: yet not I.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Amen I say to thee, that thou this day in this night, before the cocke crovv tvvise, shalt thrise deny me.
But he spake more vehemently, Although I should die together vvith thee, I vvil not denie thee. And in like maner also said they al.
And they come into a farme-place called Gethsemani. And he saith to his Disciples, Sit you here, vntil I pray.
And he taketh Peter and Iames and Iohn vvith him: and he began to feare and to be heauy.
And he saith to them, My soul is sorovvful euen vnto death: stay here, and vvatch.
And vvhen he vvas gone forvvard a litle, he fel flat vpon the ground: and he prayed that if it might be, the houre might passe from him:
and he said, Abba, Father, al things are possible to thee, transferre this chalice from me. but not that vvhich I vvil, but that vvhich thou.
And he commeth, and findeth them sleeping. And he saith to Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldst thou not vvatch one houre?
VVatch ye, and pray that you enter not into tentation. The spirit in deede is prompt, but the flesh infirme.
And going avvay againe, he prayed, saying the selfsame word.
And returning, againe he found them a sleepe (for their eies vvere heauy) and they vvist not vvhat they should ansvver him.
And he commeth the third time, and saith to them, Sleepe ye novv, and take rest, it suffiseth, the houre is come: behold the Sonne of man shal be betraied into the hands of sinners.
Arise, let vs goe. behold, he that shal betray me, is at hand.

And <cr>[1]</cr> as he vvas yet speaking, commeth Iudas Iscariote one of the Tvvelue, and vvith him a great multitude vvith swordes and clubbes, from the cheefe Priestes and the Scribes and the Auncients.
And the betrayer of him had giuen them a signe, saying, VVhomsoeuer I shal kisse, it is he, lay hold on him, and leade him vvarily.
And vvhen he vvas come, immediatly going to him, he saith, Rabbi, and he kissed him.
But they laid hands vpon him: and held him.
And one certaine man of the standers about, dravving out a svvord, smote the seruant of the cheefe priest, and cut of his eare.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering, said to them, As to a theefe are you come out vvith swordes and clubbes to apprehend me?
I was daily vvith you in the temple teaching, and you did not lay hands on me. But, that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.
Then his disciples leauing him, al fled.
And a certaine yong man folowed him clothed vvith sindon vpon the bare: & they tooke him.
But he casting of the sindon, fled from them naked.
And they brought <sc>IESVS</sc> to the cheefe Priest: and al the Priests and the Scribes and the Auncients assembled together.
And Peter folovved him a farre of euen in vnto the court of the high Priest: and he sate vvith the seruants at the fire, and vvarmed him self.
And the cheefe Priests and al the councel sought testimonie against <sc>IESVS</sc>, that they might put him to death, neither found they.
For many spake false witnes against him: and the testimonies vvere not conuenient.
And certaine rising vp, bare false vvitnes against him, saying,
That vve heard him say, <cr>[1]</cr> I wil dissolue this temple made vvith hand, and in three daies vvil I build an other not made vvith hand.
And their testimonie vvas not conuenient.
And the high Priest rising vp into the middes, asked <sc>IESVS</sc>, saying, Answerest thou nothing to these things that are obiected to thee of these?
But he held his peace and answered nothing. Againe the high Priest asked him, and said to him, Art thou Christ the sonne of the blessed God?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, I am. And you shal see the <cr>[1]</cr> Sonne of man sitting on the right hand of povver, and comming vvith the cloudes of heauen.
And the high Priest renting his garments, saith, VVhat neede vve vvitnesses any further?
You haue heard blasphemie. hovv thinke you? VVho al <na>[1]</na> condemned him to be guilty of death.

notes.text: Here we may see that they were worthily reprobated and forsaken, according to our Sauiours prediction by the parable (Mar. 12) The kingdom of God shal be taken from you &c.

verses.text: And certaine began to spit vpon him, and to couer his face, and to beate him vvith buffets, and to say vnto him, Prophecie: and the seruants gaue him blovves.
And vvhen Peter vvas in the court beneath, there commeth one of the <na>[1]</na> vvoman-seruants of the high Priest.

notes.text: He feareth not afterward Rome the Lady of the world, that in the house of Caiphas was afraid of the high Priestes wench. Leo in Natiu. Pet. & Pau. ser. 1.

verses.text: And vvhen she had seen Peter vvarming him self, beholding him she saith, And thou vvast vvith <sc>IESVS</sc> of Nazareth.
But he denied, saying, Neither knovv I, neither vvot I what thou saiest. And he vvent forth before the court: and the cocke crevve.
And againe a vvench seeing him, began to say to the standers about, That this fellovv is of them.
But he denied againe. And after a vvhile againe they that stoode by, said to Peter, Verily thou art of them: for thou art also a Galilæan.
But he began to curse and to sweare, That I knovv not this man vvhom you speake of.
And immediatly the cocke crevv againe. And Peter remembred the vvord that <sc>IESVS</sc> had said vnto him, Before the cocke crovv tvvise, thou shalt thrise deny me. And he began to vveepe.

chapters.summary: Iudas by occasion of Marie Magdalens ointment, doth sel him to the Councel of the Iewes 12 After the Paschal lambe he giueth them the bread of life (Io. 6.) in a mystical sacrifice or separation of his bodie and bloud. 27 and that night, is after his prayer, 43 taken of thee Iewes men, Iudas being their Captaine: is forsaken of the other eleuen for feare: 53 is falsly accused, and impiously condemned of the Iewes Councel, 65 and shamefully abused of them: 66 and thrise denied of Peter. Al euen as the Scriptures and him self had often foretold. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: THE PASSION according to S. Mark in these two chapters, is the Gospel at Mass upon Tuesday in the Holy Week.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> forthvvith in the morning the cheefe Priests vvith the auncients and the Scribes and the vvhole councel, consulting together, binding <sc>IESVS</sc> led and deliuered him to Pilate.

notes.text: GOOD FRIDAY.

verses.text: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Ievves? but he answering, said to him, Thou saiest.
And the cheefe Priests accused him in many things.
And Pilate againe asked him, saying, Ansvverest thou nothing? see in hovv many things they accuse thee.
But <sc>IESVS</sc> answered nothing more: so that Pilate marueled.
And vpon the festiual day he vvas vvont to release vnto them one of the prisoners vvhomsoeuer they had demaunded.
And there vvas one called Barabbas, vvhich was put in prison vvith seditious persons, vvho in a sedition had committed murder.
And when the multitude vvas come vp, they began to require according as alvvaies he did vnto them.
And Pilate ansvvered them, and said, VVil you that I release to you the King of the Ievves?
For he knevv that the cheefe Priests for enuy had deliuered him.
But the cheefe Priests moued the people, that he should release Barabbas rather to them.
And Pilate againe ansvvering, said to them, VVhat vvil you then that I doe to the King of the Ievves?
But they againe cried, Crucifie him.
And Pilate said to them, VVhy, vvhat euil hath he done? But they cried the more, Crucifie him.
And Pilate vvilling to satisfie the people, released to them Barabbas, and deliuered <sc>IESVS</sc>, hauing vvhipped him, for to be crucified.
And <cr>[1]</cr> the souldiars led him into the court of the Palace, and they call together the vvhole band:
and they clothe him in purple, and platting a crovvne of thornes, they put it vpon him.
And they began to salute him, Haile King of the Iewes.
And they smote his head vvith a reede: and they did spit on him. and bovving the knees, they adored him.
And after they had mocked him, they stripped him of the purple, and put on him his ovvne garments, and they leade him forth to crucifie him.
And they forced a certaine man that passed by, Simon a Cyrenêan comming from the countrie, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to take vp his crosse.
And they bring him into the place Golgotha, vvhich being interpreted is, The place of Caluarie.
And they gaue him to drinke vvine mingled vvith myrrhe: and he tooke it not.
And crucifying him, they deuided his garments, casting lottes vpon them, vvho should take vvhich.
And it vvas the third houre, and they crucified him.
And the title of his cause was superscribed, <sc>KING OF THE IEWES</sc>.
And vvith him they crucifie tvvo theeues: one on the right hand, and an other on his left.
And the Scripture vvas fulfilled that saith, [1] And vvith the vvicked he vvas reputed.
And they that passed by, blasphemed him, vvagging their heades, and saying, Vah, <na>[1]</na> <alt>'he that destroieth</alt>' the temple, and in three daies <na>[2]</na> <alt>'buildeth' it</alt>:

notes.text: thou that destroiest
buildest

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> saue thy self, comming dovvne from the crosse.

notes.text: So Heretikes say of the B. Sacrament, If it be Christ, let him saue him self from al iniuries.

verses.text: In like maner also the cheefe Priests mocking, said vvith the Scribes one to an other, He saued others, him self he can not saue.
Let Christ the king of Israel come dovvne novv from the crosse: that vve may see and beleeue. And they that vvere crucified vvith him, railed at him.
And vvhen it vvas the sixt houre, there vvas made darkenes vpon the vvhole earth vntil the ninthe houre.
And at the ninthe houre IESVS cried out vvith a mightie voice, saying, [1] Eloi, Eloi, lamma-sabacthani? Which is being interpreted, My God, my God, vvhy hast thou [2] forsaken me?

notes.text: See (Mat. c. 27, 46) the blasphemous exposition of Caluin and his folowers, and take heede thereof.

verses.text: And certaine of the standers about hearing, said, Behold, he calleth Elias.
And one running and filling a spunge vvith vinegre, and putting it about a reede, gaue him drinke, saying, Let be: let vs see if Elias come to take him dovvne.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> putting forth a mightie voice, gaue vp the ghost.
And the vele of the temple vvas rent in tvvo, from the toppe to the bottome.
And the Centurion that stoode ouer against him, seeing that so crying he had giuen vp the ghost, said, In deede this man vvas the sonne of God.
And there vvere also vvomen looking on a farre of: among whom vvas Marie Magdalene, and Marie the mother of Iames the lesse and of Ioseph, and Salóme:
and vvhen he vvas in Galilee, they folovved him, and ministred to him, and many other vvomen that came vp together vvith him to Hierusalem.
And vvhen euening vvas come (because it vvas the Parasceue, vvhich is the Sabboth-eue)
came Ioseph of Arimathæa a noble Senatour, vvho him self also vvas expecting the kingdom of God: and he vvent in boldly to Pilate, and asked the body of <sc>IESVS</sc>.
But Pilate marueled if he vvere novv dead. And sending for the Centurion, asked him if he vvere novv dead.
And vvhen he vnderstoode by the Centurion, he gaue the body to Ioseph.
And Ioseph bying sindon, and taking him dovvne, vvrapped him in the sindon, and laid him in a monument, that vvas hevved out of a rocke. And he rolled a stone to the doore of the monument.
And Marie Magdalene and Marie of Ioseph beheld vvhere he vvas laid.

chapters.summary: The cheefe of the Iewes accuse him to Pilate the Gentil. 6 And (he seeking to deliuer him) they persuade the common people (who hitherto were alwaies ready to defend him) not only to preferre the murderer Barabbas, but also to crie Crucifige (to the reprobation of the whole nation.) 16 After many illusions, 20 he is crucified by the Gentils. 29 Which the Iewes seing, do triumph as if they had now the victorie. 33 But euen then by many wonderful workes he declareth his might, 42 and finally is buried honorably.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> vvhen the Sabboth vvas past, Marie Magdalene and Marie of Iames, and Salôme bought spices, that comming they might anoint <sc>IESVS</sc>.

notes.text: The Gospel upon Easter day.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> And very early the first of the Sabboths, they come to the monument: the sunne being novv risen.

notes.text: EASTER DAY.

verses.text: And they said one to an other, VVho shal roll vs backe the stone from the doore of the monument?
And looking, they savv the stone rolled backe. for it vvas very great.
And entring into the monument, they saw a yong man sitting on the right hand, couered vvith a white robe: and they vvere astonied.
VVho saith to them, Be not dismaied: you seeke <sc>IESVS</sc> of Nazareth, that vvas crucified: he is risen, he is not here, behold the place vvhere they laid him.
But goe, tel his Disciples and <cr>[1]</cr> Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there you shal see him, <na>[2]</na> as he told you. ⊢

notes.text: Peter is named in special (as often els where) for prerogatiue. · Mr. 14, 28.

verses.text: But they going forth, fled from the monument. for trembling and feare had inuaded them: and they said nothing to any body. for they vvere afraid.
And he rising early the first of the Sabboth, <cr>[1]</cr> appeared first to Marie Magdalene, <cr>[2]</cr> out of vvhom he had cast seuen deuils.
She went and told them that had been vvith him, that vvere mourning and vveeping.
And they hearing that he vvas aliue and had been seen of her, did not beleeue.
And <cr>[1]</cr> after this he appeared in an other shape to tvvo of them vvalking, as they vvere going into the countrie.
and they going told the rest: neither them did they beleeue.

<cr>[1]</cr> Last <na>[2]</na> he appeared to those eleuen as they sate at the table: and he exprobrated their incredulity and hardnes of hart, because they did not beleeue them that had seen him risen againe.

notes.text: The Gospel upon the Ascension day. And for some Martyrs.

verses.text: And he said to them, <cr>[1]</cr> Going into the vvhole vvorld preach the Gospel to al creatures.
He that beleeueth and is baptized, shal be saued: but he that beleeueth not, shal be condemned.
And them that beleeue these signes shal folow: In my name shal they cast out deuils, They shal speake vvith nevv tonges,
Serpents shal they take avvay, And if they drinke any deadly thing, it shal not hurt them, They shal <na>[1]</na> impose hands vpon the sicke: and they shal be vvhole.

notes.text: Miracles the Church by imposition of hand.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And so our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> after he spake vnto them, <na>[2]</na> vvas assumpted into heauen, and sate on the right hand of God.

notes.text: The Ascension.

verses.text: But they going forth preached euery vvhere: our Lord working vvithal, and confirming the vvord vvith signes that folowed. ⊢

chapters.summary: The third day, to three women at his Sepulcher, an Angel telleth that he is risen, and wil (as he promised Mar. 14, 28.) shew him self in Galilee. 9 The same day he appeareth to Marie Magdalene, afterward to two Disciples: yet the Eleuen wil not beleeue it, vntil to them also he appeareth. 15 To whom hauing giuen commission into al nations, with power also of Miracles, he ascendeth, and they plant his Church euery where.
